keywords: how do i know i love
entries.answer: When you think about their happiness before yours, and you pray for them, that is a good sign. Take your time.
Family is home, love, support and prayer. Keep close to your family, and thank them for every small help.
Prayer is talking to God like a father. A good verse to remember is Jeremiah 29:11: God knows the plans He has for you, plans to give you hope and a future.

To apply to a university, usually you:
1. Go to the university website or admissions office
2. Fill the application form
3. Attach your Grade 12 results and NRC
4. Pay the application fee
5. Submit before the deadline

Dates and fees change every year, so please confirm with the official office. Which university and programme do you want?

HELSB means Higher Education Loans and Scholarships Board. It gives student loans and bursaries in Zambia. Usually you need acceptance at a public university first.

To apply: use the HELSB online portal, fill the form, upload your documents (acceptance letter, Grade 12 results, NRC, parents' NRC) and submit before the deadline. Apply early, be honest, keep copies.

Which part is hard for you?
I wish I could promise that, but I cannot. Loan awards depend on HELSB's official selection. What I can do is help you understand the requirements and prepare your application well.

According to the HELSB website, student loans are given to undergraduate students joining UNZA, CBU, KMU, MKU, MU, CHAU and KNU. Yes, KMU is on that list. Policies can change, so please confirm on helsb.gov.zm.

An appeal is a formal letter asking them to look at your case again, when you were not accepted or not awarded. Write calmly and honestly, say what happened, and attach proof. Don't give up, many people try again.
Screening is when the university or HELSB checks your original documents with their own eyes. Carry all your originals and copies, and arrive early.

ZAQA is the Zambia Qualifications Authority. It checks that qualifications are real, especially foreign results. ECZ results are checked through ECZ. Tell me which one you need (ECZ or ZAQA) and I will guide you step by step.
After you are accepted, apply for accommodation through the student affairs office and pay the fee. Apply early and keep your receipt.
A deadline is the last day to submit. If you miss it, you may lose your chance. Do not wait for the last day, and I will not guess dates for you. Please check the official notice.
TPIN means Taxpayer Identification Number, from ZRA. Go to a ZRA office or the ZRA website with your NRC and register. It is free. Get it early, because you may need it for HELSB.

HELSB is not the only way. There are scholarships, bursaries, sponsorships and grants. Always check if it is fully funded, partly funded or tuition only. And never pay a strange fee to get a scholarship. A real one has an official source.
Hahaha, even the bank account needs encouragement sometimes! But do not give up. Let us look at cheaper schools, chances to apply, and any financial help. What programme do you want?
Please never share your password, PIN or OTP with me, Moses or anyone in chat. Keep them private. For account problems, use the official website.
You can pay with Airtel Money or MTN MoMo. I cannot confirm a payment myself. It counts only after it shows in the payment records. After paying, send your proof to Moses on WhatsApp.
A request is either submitted, pending, processing or completed. I cannot say it is completed unless the records show it. Please send your name and request details to Moses on WhatsApp.
No problem. Tap the green WhatsApp button below to reach Moses. It is best for serious or special cases.
You are most welcome! God bless you. Ask me anything else, any time.

I am an AI, so I do not have a family or an age. Moses Ntembwa (MR TEES) is a young student at Kapasa Makasa University in Chinsali, studying Information Systems and Business Analytics, and the founder of MR TEES Education Services. For personal questions, message him on WhatsApp (0771043702).
According to the HELSB FAQ, the interest rate on student loans is 10 percent amortized per year. Always read your loan agreement for the exact terms.
HELSB loans cater for tuition fees, accommodation fees, meal allowances, book allowances and project allowances.
You can apply for both a loan and a scholarship, but HELSB says an applicant cannot be awarded both.
Students repay their loans one year after leaving school. The exact terms are in your loan agreement, so please read it carefully.
HELSB asks applicants to make sure all documents are certified by the relevant authorities before they submit.
